findings.title: VIEW permission incorrectly grants global group manage permission
findings.body: canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) against the all-groups resource, so an administrator granted only the view scope for all groups passes requireManage() checks such as creating a top-level group in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup. Group creation/modification must require MANAGE only; VIEW should grant read access. This is a privilege-escalation bug not covered by the tests, which only verify creation with MANAGE.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns and evaluates authorization-resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: For V2 group resources the group ID is stored as the resource name (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() and getOrCreateResource creates the resource with that as its name), while Resource.getId() is the authorization store's own resource UUID. This code passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission(String groupId, ...), which looks up resources by name, so specific-group resources are never found and evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource. It also adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set, but callers in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource and getUsersCount expect actual group IDs for filtering users by group membership. The result is wrong user visibility/counts for admins with view-members/manage-members on specific groups.

findings.title: hasPermission can throw NullPointerException when the all-groups resource does not exist
findings.body: When no specific group resource is found, the code loads the all-groups resource via getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later constructs a ResourcePermission with it, without a null check. If the Groups type resource is absent (for example the resource server was initialized before it was created, or admin permissions resources were not (re)initialized), every canView/canManage/canViewMembers check for a group without its own resource throws an NPE instead of denying access.

findings.title: Existing FGAP V2 realms never get the new Groups scopes/resource
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null, and this is the only place shown that creates the schema's scopes and all-resource-type resources. Realms that already enabled admin permissions before this change therefore keep a resource server with only the old Users/Clients scopes and resources: the Groups all-resource and the manage-membership/manage-members/view-members scopes are never added. Creating Groups scope permissions in such realms then fails scope resolution/validation, and group evaluations hit the missing-resource path, so the feature only works for newly initialized realms unless a migration/backfill is added.
